Success means capturing more legitimate demand without growing fraud, support burden, or finance complexity. Works with payments engineering, risk, store operations and finance; those teams own integration acceptance, reader readiness, loss review and settlement exceptions.
careAbout: Maximizing successful payment conversion on every checkout session
Adding local payment methods without long integration cycles
Reducing authorization failures caused by issuer, SCA, or orchestration gaps
Keeping refunds, disputes, and reconciliation manageable as volume scales
Using one platform across online, mobile, and in-person commerce
Compare Stripe, Adyen and other routes using the same merchant cohort, total cost, loss and cash-availability measures
winsThem: Hosted and embeddable checkout surfaces that ship quickly
Strong authorization optimization and payment-method coverage
Unified reporting across charges, refunds, disputes, and payouts
Built-in fraud controls that protect conversion rather than only block volume
A clear path from online payments into Terminal and finance operations
Documented product and region eligibility, recoverable integrations and independently reconciled pilot results
theirFear: Losing revenue because checkout conversion degrades silently by market or payment method
Adding operational overhead every time they launch a new country or channel
Creating finance, support, or fraud problems while chasing growth

customerJourneyStories.name: Global checkout expansion without conversion loss
customerJourneyStories.summary: A commerce GM wants to add countries, payment methods, and physical touchpoints while protecting conversion and keeping finance operations understandable.

stages.narrative: Declining conversion in a market or a store rollout triggers a payments review.
The GM encounters Stripe through an ecommerce integration partner, a peer merchant reference or payment-performance material, then shortlists it alongside Adyen and other relevant providers.
Payments engineering and finance compare method coverage, contractual liability, reader coverage, total cost and migration effort; risk agrees loss guardrails and the test cohort before a pilot.
A limited market or store pilot runs alongside the incumbent; exit criteria include agreed conversion and loss performance, reconciled settlements and a tested rollback.
Growth and operations review payment cohorts together, while store teams own device exceptions and finance owns settlement mismatches.
Renewal or expansion follows sustained net customer value, reliable operations and demonstrated support across the next eligible market or channel.

customerJourneyStories.name: Usage-based monetization without finance breakage
customerJourneyStories.summary: A RevOps lead wants to add usage pricing and invoice complexity without sacrificing collection rates, tax correctness, or month-end trust.

stages.narrative: A new usage or AI pricing model exposes spreadsheet corrections, customer bill disputes or a slow finance close.
The lead finds Stripe Billing and Metronome through developer documentation, finance peers or an implementation partner; Orb/Adyen, Chargebee and Paddle surface as different alternatives.
Product and finance compare contracts, credits, tax responsibility, accounting handoffs and compatibility. They decide whether to remain merchant of record and define migration acceptance.
A representative subscription and usage cohort runs in parallel; invoice totals, corrections, credit balances and exports must reconcile before collection is switched.
Revenue operations controls price versions and collections; engineering monitors usage ingestion and the controller signs off accounting outputs.
The business expands usage when pricing changes stay explainable and collection/close effort falls; renewal depends on measured outcomes, not suite attachment alone.

customerJourneyStories.name: Marketplace activation and payout reliability at scale
customerJourneyStories.summary: A platform payments GM needs to activate more supply, move money to counterparties predictably, and keep operator controls strong as the platform expands internationally.

stages.narrative: Seller activation stalls, payout complaints rise or a new platform market changes responsibility and eligibility requirements.
The GM discovers Connect and Adyen for Platforms through platform peers, vertical SaaS partners or payment-provider discussions.
Legal, risk and engineering compare account roles, negative-balance liability, regional eligibility, fees and recipient support; they define an onboarding and payout pilot.
A bounded eligible seller cohort completes verification, a live transaction and a reconciled payout, including tested document-remediation and payout-return paths.
The platform monitors capability changes and funds flows daily; recipient support can explain blocked onboarding, fees and delayed funds.
Retention follows predictable seller activation and usable earnings with sustainable platform economics; optional financial products require separate eligibility and adoption evidence.

customerJourneyStories.name: Trust the platform with verification and earnings
customerJourneyStories.summary: The seller joins a platform to reach customers but needs confidence in its onboarding and payout process.

stages.narrative: The seller joins a platform to reach customers but needs confidence in its onboarding and payout process.
A platform invitation, seller peer or partner explains the payment service and what the seller must provide.
The seller reviews fees, payout windows, data requests, liability terms and support access before agreeing to the service.
The seller completes a small first transaction and checks that net funds arrive at the verified destination as promised.
Earnings statements and actionable exception notices become part of routine business administration.
The seller stays when access to earnings and support are dependable; any financial-product offer is evaluated separately.

customerJourneyStories.summary: Fragmented balances or recurring payout failures prompt a review of treasury operations.

stages.narrative: Fragmented balances or recurring payout failures prompt a review of treasury operations.
The controller learns about Stripe Treasury, Adyen Intelligent Money Movement and Airwallex from banking partners, finance peers or enterprise account teams.
Finance and legal compare account ownership, entity/country eligibility, funding, liability, FX and reporting; they set acceptance criteria for the chosen account arrangement.
An eligible entity funds a limited account, pays a small recipient cohort and reconciles statements and returns before migration expands.
Treasury uses controlled approvals and daily cash views; the controller closes against matched source and external records.
The business renews when cash access and close quality remain predictable; broader regions or delegated spending require separate approval and product availability.
